program_overview.title: TypeScript Programming Masterclass
program_overview.tagline: The language modern teams actually write: JavaScript foundations, the type system as a superpower, then typed React and Node end to end.
program_overview.description:
TypeScript won: new frontend and most serious Node work is written in it, and the type system, learned properly, is not bureaucracy but a superpower: bugs caught at compile time, refactors that stop being scary, editors that finish your thoughts. This live online masterclass builds it honestly: JavaScript foundations first (TypeScript is JavaScript underneath), then the type system to real depth, generics, narrowing, utility types, the honest limits, then typed application development: React with TypeScript the way product teams write it, and Node backends with types end to end. A finale month ships a full-stack typed capstone and sits the final exam.

The pace is honest: ten teaching months at two live classes a week plus four to six hours of practice, with two more in hand. Problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest.
what_makes_this_different: JavaScript first, honestly: TypeScript without JS depth is decoration
The type system as a skill: generics and narrowing understood, not copy-pasted
Typed both ends: React and Node with types flowing end to end
Real-team habits: strictness levels, migration judgment, when any is a lie
An honest 10-month arc with 2 months in hand
Real assessment: weekly problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams and a final exam with a free retest

phase_1_foundation.title: PHASE 1: Foundation & TypeScript Fundamentals (Months 1-3, Weeks 1-13)
phase_1_foundation.description: Build rock-solid JavaScript and TypeScript fundamentals. Learn programming logic, master TypeScript syntax, type systems, and create your first applications.

week_1.title: Introduction to Programming & JavaScript Basics
topics: What is programming? Introduction to software development
JavaScript ecosystem: browsers, Node.js, runtime environments
Why TypeScript? Benefits over plain JavaScript
Installing Node.js and npm package manager
Setting up development environment: VS Code with TypeScript extensions
Understanding IDE features: IntelliSense, debugging, extensions
Your first JavaScript program: Hello World
Running JavaScript in browser console and Node.js
JavaScript coding conventions and naming standards
Console methods: log, error, warn, table
projects: Hello World variations with personalized messages
week_1.practice: Daily: 30 min JavaScript syntax practice, write 5-10 simple programs

week_2_3.title: Variables, Data Types & Operators
topics: Variables: var, let, const - differences and best practices
Primitive data types: string, number, boolean, null, undefined, symbol, bigint
Type coercion: implicit and explicit conversion
Optional chaining operator (?.) and its uses
projects: Area and perimeter calculator for shapes
week_2_3.practice: Solve 30 problems on variables, data types, and operators

week_4_5.title: Control Flow & Functions
projects: Number guessing game with attempts limit
week_4_5.practice: Solve 40 control flow and function problems

week_6_7.title: Arrays, Objects & ES6+ Features
topics: Array methods: push, pop, shift, unshift, splice
Array iteration: forEach, map, filter, reduce
Array methods: find, findIndex, some, every, includes
projects: Array statistics calculator (sum, average, min, max)
Linear search and binary search implementation
Sorting algorithms: bubble sort, selection sort
week_6_7.practice: Create 25 programs using arrays and objects, solve 30 problems

week_8_9.title: TypeScript Fundamentals & Setup
topics: Introduction to TypeScript: static typing benefits
Compiler options: target, module, strict mode
Enum types: numeric and string enums
Any type: when and when not to use
Unknown type: safe alternative to any
Type assertions: as and angle-bracket syntax
Literal types: string, number, boolean literals
week_8_9.practice: Convert 10 JavaScript programs to TypeScript with proper types

week_10_11.title: Interfaces, Type Aliases & Advanced Types
topics: Interface vs type alias: when to use which
Type guards: typeof, instanceof, in operator
Nullable types and strict null checks
week_10_11.practice: Build 15 projects using interfaces and advanced types

week_12_13.title: Generics & Advanced TypeScript
topics: Generic utility types: Partial, Required, Readonly
Conditional types with extends and infer
Module systems: ES modules in TypeScript
projects: Generic data structure library (Stack, Queue, LinkedList)
PHASE 1 MINI CAPSTONE: CLI Task Manager
Features: Tasks, categories, priorities, file persistence, full TypeScript typing
week_12_13.practice: Create 15 generic utilities, solve 30 generics problems
week_12_13.assessment: Phase 1 exam: a practical build defended live, plus a written paper mixing this phase with everything before it

faqs.question: What does this TypeScript course cover?
faqs.answer: JavaScript foundations first (TypeScript is JavaScript underneath), the type system to real depth, generics, narrowing, utility types and their honest limits, then typed application development on both ends: React with TypeScript as product teams write it, and Node APIs with contracts the frontend shares. A finale month ships a strict-mode-clean full-stack capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn TypeScript properly?
faqs.answer: Ten months of teaching at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, with two more months in hand for learners who need them. The three teaching phases build the skill and its real-world application; the finale month ships a capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new material with earlier topics, each phase ends with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Should I learn JavaScript first, or start directly with TypeScript?
faqs.answer: This course settles it: you learn JavaScript properly inside it, then add types. Starting with TypeScript syntax over weak JavaScript produces developers who fight the compiler; learning JS first then typing it produces developers the compiler helps. That order is the course.

faqs.question: What are the fees?
faqs.answer: Group classes are ₹1,499 per month, with 2 live classes a week in batches capped at 10 learners. A mini batch of 3-4 learners is ₹2,999 per month, and personal 1-on-1 classes are ₹4,999 per month. International learners pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency.
